parameters.content:
## Fernhill weekly ops report
Pulls last week and the week before from Stripe, HubSpot, Zendesk, Linear and GitHub.
**Code** computes every metric, delta and anomaly. A failed or empty source is *missing*, never zero.
**The model** only writes the narrative from that JSON. **Code** then checks every number in it; one rewrite, then a numbers-only fallback.
Owen gets a DM. **#all-hands only after Owen approves** (Wait node, header auth).
The grey "(live)" nodes are the production path; the HTTP nodes above them hit the mock SaaS server.

nodes.name: Stripe (live)
nodes.notes: Production: Stripe credential; page through events for the two weeks, then feed Compute metrics the same shape.

nodes.name: HubSpot (live)
nodes.notes: Production: HubSpot private-app credential; search deals by createdate / closedate.

nodes.name: Zendesk (live)
nodes.notes: Production: Zendesk API token; tickets created in the window with metrics sideloaded.

nodes.name: Linear (live)
nodes.notes: Production: Linear API key; issues created/completed in the window with labels and priority.

nodes.name: GitHub (live)
nodes.notes: Production: GitHub token; deployments + statuses for environment=production.

messageValues.message: You are a helpful assistant. Write a short, upbeat weekly ops summary for the COO of Fernhill Software from the data below. Highlight wins and anything notable from support tickets. One headline, then bullets.

nodes.name: Slack: DM @owen (live)
nodes.notes: Production path: attach a Slack credential, enable this node, and disable the mock HTTP sibling.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ...$('Build report').first().json, execution_id: $execution.id, approve_url: $execution.resumeUrl, how_to_approve: 'POST {"approved": true, "approver": "owen"} to approve_url with the X-Approval-Token header. Anything else, or no answer in 48 hours, means #all-hands is not posted.' }) }}
